privacy.title: Our data policy
privacy.subtitle: What we ask for, what we don't, and how we keep and delete your data.
privacy.intro: Tasami Alwataniyah Establishment provides government transaction and tech services to individuals and businesses in Saudi Arabia. This page explains in plain language how we handle your data on the website, the request form and WhatsApp.

s1.title: 1. What we ask for
s1.body: Only what your transaction needs: name and mobile number, client type, city and requested service, then the documents the official authority requires (such as ID, iqama or CR copies). We tell you the list before starting.

s2.title: 2. What we don't ask for
s2.body: We never ask for your bank card details on WhatsApp or the website, and we don't ask for documents unrelated to your transaction. If a transaction needs an authorisation on an official platform, we explain its type and duration before you grant it.

s3.title: 3. How we use your data
s3.body: Only to complete your transaction and contact you about it. We share it with the official authority handling your transaction when needed. We never sell it or use it for other purposes.

s4.title: 4. Request form and tracking
s4.body: When you use the request form we store the service, city, client type and your mobile number if you enter it, and give you an order number. The tracking page shows only the status and service name, never personal data.

s5.title: 5. Analytics and ads
s5.body: We use analytics tools such as Google Analytics, Meta Pixel and TikTok Pixel to count visits, WhatsApp button clicks and form submissions, to improve the site and our ads. We don't send your name, number or documents to these tools.

s6.title: 6. Retention and deletion
s6.body: We keep your data and documents for the duration of the transaction and as required by law afterwards. You can ask for a copy, a correction or deletion at any time on WhatsApp, and we delete unless a legal obligation prevents it.

s7.title: 7. Contact us
s7.body: For any question about your data, message either department on WhatsApp or call us during working hours.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.subtitle: Government fees vs. service fees, rejection and cancellation, in plain language.
terms.intro: These terms govern your dealings with Tasami Alwataniyah Establishment through the website or WhatsApp. By sending a request and accepting a quote you agree to them.

s1.title: 1. Nature of the service
s1.body: We are a services establishment, not a government entity. We complete transactions on your behalf through the official platforms and build tech solutions as agreed. Acceptance or rejection is decided by the official authority.

s2.title: 2. Quote
s2.body: Each service has its own quote, sent within an hour during working hours, showing our fee, the expected duration and the required documents. We don't start before you approve the quote.

s3.title: 3. Government fees vs. service fees
s3.body: Government fees (such as renewal fees, levies or fines) are paid to the authority and are separate from our service fee. The quote lists each item separately.

s4.title: 4. Your responsibilities
s4.body: Provide correct, valid information and documents and respond to document requests on time. Delays or rejections caused by incomplete or incorrect information are not Tasami's responsibility.

s5.title: 5. If a transaction is rejected
s5.body: We review the reason with you, fix what is needed and resubmit as agreed in the quote. Government fees paid to the authority are subject to that authority's rules.

s6.title: 6. Cancellation
s6.body: You can cancel before work starts at no charge. After work starts, completed work is charged according to the quote, and government fees already paid are not refundable.

s7.title: 7. Timelines
s7.body: The duration in the quote is an estimate that depends on the authority and its systems. We update you at every step and tell you immediately about any delay outside our control.

s8.title: 8. Governing law
s8.body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and Saudi courts have jurisdiction over any dispute.
